For example, I might eat 1 slice of bread, with a table spoon of peanut butter for breakfast. Or 1 granola bar. Then 1-2 boiled eggs for dinner, and that's all I will eat for that day.

The biggest benefit - besides weight loss, which has already been stressed - is the energy and psychological sharpness. Staying sort of adrenalized all day keeps you on your toes, and I've found I think better. Much, much better. No more (really, no more) of that mid afternoon brain fog or sleepiness after lunch. You're just "on it" all day.

The caveat, for me personally, is that when you do finally get that meal in at the end of the day, you're done. But that is the beauty of this; being in that adrenal state during the day is how human beings evolved to operate. It means that when you eat later in the evening, that you are actually tired and ready to sleep at night. It's a natural cycle and helps to regulate your diurnal rhythms. This is good for hormone production.

One thing to note: I tried IF while also doing strict keto, and that destroyed my hormone levels. Fat loss is enhanced by this, but I also found it wasn't sustainable. I developed the "keto rash", and my libido flat-lined. I felt the effects of low testosterone, except for the hours after a workout.

People think that testosterone production is all about fat - to an extent it does require cholesterol. But testosterone exists in a sensitive dynamic with dopamine and cortisol levels. If you are going to be in the adrenalized state all day, your cortisol naturally elevates. It feels good. Lowers pain. Keeps you feeling secure. But you have to lower that at night with carbohydrate. If your adrenocorticoids are elevated all day, your testosterone will be low. That's just a fact.

You have to recover. That's the biggest lesson I'd take: IF is about accentuating the cycle of deprivation-RECOVERY. Don't eat shit, but make sure you are getting carbohydrate.
